Production Engineer, Tooling Asset Management 

 Introduction to the Job

 As a Production Engineer, Tooling Asset Management, you will help keep advanced manufacturing equipment reliable, organized, and ready for production. You will support the management of tooling assets, maintenance activities, spare parts, and technical documentation.

 This entry-level opportunity is well suited for recent graduates or early-career engineers interested in manufacturing. Your work will help improve equipment reliability, production efficiency, and the processes used to build ASML’s advanced technology.

 Role and Responsibilities 

 As a Production Engineer, Tooling Asset Management, you will work closely with engineering, maintenance, and manufacturing teams. You will combine hands-on production support with data analysis and continuous improvement.

 Maintain tooling asset information, maintenance documentation, and equipment records within maintenance management systems.
 Develop and maintain preventive and operator-led maintenance tasks that support equipment reliability and availability.
 Coordinate tooling spare parts, equipment calibration, service agreements, and maintenance requirements.
 Monitor maintenance work orders and key performance indicators to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
 Support production tooling issues through troubleshooting, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and qualification testing.
 Improve manufacturing processes by supporting quality, lean manufacturing, cycle time, and labor-efficiency initiatives.
 Create and update manufacturing procedures, work instructions, equipment documentation, and engineering change information.
 
 Education and Experience
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, industrial, manufacturing engineering, or a related engineering field.
 Zero to two years of experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment. Relevant internship experience is valued.
 Basic knowledge of manufacturing processes, preventive maintenance, equipment reliability, and quality principles.
 Familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems or similar equipment maintenance systems.
 Familiarity with computer-aided design tools such as SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or Siemens NX.
 Basic understanding of data analysis, statistical process control, Lean, or Six Sigma principles.
 Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and technical documentation.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
 
 Skills

 Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
 To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
 Approach technical problems with curiosity, analytical thinking, and a structured problem-solving mindset.
 Collaborate effectively with manufacturing, engineering, maintenance, quality, and other cross-functional teams.
 Communicate technical information clearly through written documentation and conversations with colleagues.
 Organize detailed asset, maintenance, and engineering information accurately.
 Take ownership of assignments and follow through on agreed actions.
 Adapt quickly and remain open to learning new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing processes.
 Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, quality, safety, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Work safely while following established quality and compliance requirements.
 
 This Production Engineer, Tooling Asset Management position provides an opportunity to build a strong foundation in manufacturing engineering while contributing directly to equipment performance and production reliability. As you grow in the Production Engineer, Tooling Asset Management role, you will gain exposure to maintenance strategy, troubleshooting, data analysis, and continuous improvement.
